rows.note: TC-01 and the published-manifest reader hold ownership-input-changed when a declared input drifts, and a successful rebuild is not this row.
RB-03 is consumption of a new file under a registered prefix, not a refusal, and TC-04 is a refusal that holds silent absorption after planning.
RB-18 and IFIT-1 hold ownership-missing at the rebuild and reader entry points when the referenced object is absent.
The store rehash reads tampered CAS bytes as absent, so the reader integrity hold is not reached through createDiskStore and is not a distinct broken-index reader reason.
RB-15 holds an omitted required edge, not a version order, and the dependency comparison propagates a changed result without refusing a version.
No opened assertion names an invalid generation and refuses it, and G3-02 and G3-03 were not renamed into this row.
The independent-scope read stays ready while the affected scope holds, and RB-20 keeps another scope readable after a primary hold.

rows.clause: shared manifest corruption holds dependent reads
rows.note: No opened assertion shows corruption of a shared manifest holding its dependent reads, and missing-artifact and foreign-identity rollback were not stretched into this row.
The opened ownership tests do not call branch protection, and existing CI is not assumed to call a new updater.
87abf90956 also holds RB-07 (recipe-a-2) and RB-11 (recipe-b-2), so it is not the door, and the recipe-file version comparison is not a comparison to the baseline receipt.
Rebuild returns a private candidate and does not emit, and a candidate is not a publication refusal.
The actual emit refuses without a ratification token and publishes once one is present.
G3-03 refuses a foreign identity replacement and a reopened load still returns the previous projection, while the same test says the untrusted seam blanks on read and is not this citation.
The same independent-scope assertions cited for AC09-07 keep an unrelated scope usable, and no additional test was added.

rows.clause: generated boundaries change only through generators
rows.note: The boundary check expects a diagnostic containing "Stale generated Atlas boundary" after a whitespace write, which is a byte-reproduction check and not an assertion that a generated boundary cannot be hand-edited.
